question: In which year was the demonetisation of 500- and 1000-rupees notes announced in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2016**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Government of India announced the demonetisation of ₹500 and ₹1000 currency notes on **8th November 2016**.
 
• This announcement was made by the then Prime Minister of India, **Narendra Modi**, in a televised address to the nation.
 
• The demonetised notes ceased to be legal tender with immediate effect, except for a few essential services until **30th December 2016**.
 
• The primary objectives of demonetisation were to **curb black money, counterfeit currency, and terrorist financing**.
 
• New ₹500 and ₹2000 currency notes were introduced by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) as replacements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Black Money:**

 
 
• Black money refers to income illegally obtained or not declared for tax purposes.
 
• Demonetisation aimed to bring undeclared money into the formal economy by encouraging people to deposit cash in banks.
 
 
 
• **Counterfeit Currency:**
 
 
• Counterfeit currency is fake money intended to deceive and manipulate the financial system.
 
• The demonetisation initiative targeted the circulation of fake ₹500 and ₹1000 notes, which were being used for illegal activities.
 
 
 
• **Digital Transactions:**
 
 
• Demonetisation led to a significant increase in **digital payments** as people turned to alternative modes of payment.
 
• The government promoted platforms like UPI, BHIM, and e-wallets to reduce dependence on cash.
 
 
 
• **Criticism and Challenges:**
 
 
• The demonetisation move faced criticism for causing disruptions in the economy, particularly in the **informal sector**.
 
• There were long queues at banks and ATMs, and the sudden cash crunch affected daily wage workers and small businesses.
